title: Beautiful sky over Paranal
caption: The Milky Way over the VLT Auxiliary Telescopes, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: The Milky Way hangs above three of the four VLT Auxiliary Telescopes in this early-morning view of the sky over Paranal, home of ESO's Very Large Telescope. The camera faces east, and the centre of the Milky Way lies just below the middle of the picture.

Each Auxiliary Telescope is 1.8 metres across. They observe at the same time, using interferometry to see as sharply as a single telescope as wide as the greatest distance between them, in this case 48 metres. The larger 8.2-metre Unit Telescopes are usually used on their own, so the four Auxiliary Telescopes were added to make full use of the interferometry laboratory.
The constellations in view are Ophiuchus, the snake-holder; Sagittarius, the archer; Scorpius, the scorpion; and Triangulum Australe, the southern triangle.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken with a camera at an ESO site, in visible light. The camera settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long camera exposure gathers far more light than the eye can, so the Milky Way and faint stars appear brighter and richer than they would to someone standing there.

explore: The photograph was taken by Yuri Beletsky early one morning, facing east towards the centre of the Milky Way. ESO also made it available as a mounted print in its shop.
alt: The bright centre of the Milky Way above three telescopes on a mountain platform.
